questions.q: What should determine how a cluster is sized for a specific job?
options: The job's actual workload shape — shuffle-heavy versus scan-heavy — not a generic instance-size guess
Always picking the largest instance type available, regardless of the job
The number of notebooks attached to the cluster
The color-coded label given to the cluster in the workspace UI
questions.explain: A cluster sized right for one workload shape can be badly wrong for another shape, even at the same total core count.

questions.q: What does a shuffle-heavy workload typically bottleneck on?
options: Network and disk I/O moving data between nodes during joins and wide aggregations
The number of notebooks a user has open
The cluster's Photon acceleration setting exclusively
The color scheme of the Databricks workspace UI
questions.explain: Wide transformations like joins and high-cardinality GROUP BY move large amounts of data between nodes, which is where the real bottleneck sits.

questions.q: What does `min_workers` in an autoscaling configuration protect against?
options: Cold-start latency — every job trigger on a zero-worker cluster would otherwise wait for new nodes to spin up
A job consuming an unlimited compute budget
Data becoming stale between reads
A skewed shuffle partition slowing down a query
questions.explain: A floor of running workers keeps a baseline ready instead of scaling from zero on every trigger.

options: An unexpectedly large or runaway job scaling out to consume far more compute budget than intended
The cluster running out of local disk space for logs
A notebook losing its connection to the cluster
Photon acceleration failing to activate
questions.explain: The ceiling caps how far autoscaling can grow, bounding the worst-case cost of an unusually large or runaway job.

questions.q: Why doesn't a bigger cluster help a job bottlenecked on one severely skewed shuffle partition?
options: That one oversized partition still runs as a single task on a single core, regardless of how many other cores are available
Bigger clusters always cost more without exception
Skew only affects clusters running Photon
A skewed partition automatically triggers cluster auto-termination
questions.explain: Adding more nodes doesn't split a single task's data for it — actually fixing skew (e.g., via AQE) is what addresses the real bottleneck.
